memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now when all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings along the coast heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed over, their hearts melted in fear and they no longer had the courage to face the Israelites. — Josh 5:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The news of the Jordan crossing spread like wildfire among the kings of Canaan, and their reaction was total dread. Their "hearts melted in fear," and their courage drained away. What God had done at the river became a mighty witness to the whole land before a single battle was fought.

Notice something important. God went ahead of Israel and prepared the way by working in the hearts of their enemies. Before Israel lifted a sword, God had already softened the ground of victory. Sometimes the greatest battles are won by God long before we ever arrive on the scene. He is working ahead of us in ways we cannot see.

This should quiet our anxious hearts. We often march toward our challenges imagining we must conquer everything by our own strength. But the God who dried up the Jordan is already at work in the situation before us — moving hearts, arranging circumstances, going before us.

The same Lord who prepared the way for Israel prepares the way for His people still. In Christ, we are told, "if God is for us, who can be against us?" (Rom 8:31). We do not walk into our battles alone or unprepared. The God who goes before us has already been at work, and His victory is sure.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to face challenges as if everything depends on your own strength?
2. Can you recall a time God had clearly "gone before" you and prepared the way?
3. How does it calm your heart to know God is already at work in what lies ahead?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You go before me and work in ways I cannot see. Quiet my anxious heart with the truth that You have already prepared the way. Amen.
